skill.name: obsidian-cli
skill.description: Interact with Obsidian vaults using the Obsidian CLI to read, create, search, and manage notes, tasks, properties, and more. Also supports plugin and theme development with commands to reload plugins, run JavaScript, capture errors, take screenshots, and inspect the DOM. Use when the user asks to interact with their Obsidian vault, manage notes, search vault content, perform vault operations from the command line, or develop and debug Obsidian plugins and themes.
skill.summary: Use the Obsidian CLI to manage vault notes, searches, tasks, and plugin debugging.
skill.author: kepano

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick alerts are Markdown formatting, but several examples intentionally invoke the Obsidian CLI. Main concerns are vault mutation, sensitive developer output, and app-context JavaScript evaluation; no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript evaluation is documented without guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before obsidian eval, CDP, or debugger commands. Avoid eval for routine note operations.

remediation.issue: Vault-changing commands can create, append, and update notes.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the target vault, target file, and intended change before create, append, daily append, or property commands.

remediation.issue: Developer outputs can expose local vault or plugin data.
remediation.suggestion: Limit screenshots, DOM text, console output, and clipboard use to the requested scope. Do not copy sensitive output by default.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger broad static command warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Document which commands are read-only, mutating, or developer-only so users can review risk before execution.

static_findings.snippet: Use the `obsidian` CLI to interact with a running Obsidian instance. Requires Obsidian to be open.
Run `obsidian help` to see all available commands. This is always up to date. Full docs: https://hel
**Parameters** take a value with `=`. Quote values with spaces:
For multiline content use `\n` for newline and `\t` for tab.
Many commands accept `file` or `path` to target a file. Without either, the active file is used.
- `file=<name>` — resolves like a wikilink (name only, no path or extension needed)
- `path=<path>` — exact path from vault root, e.g. `folder/note.md`
Commands target the most recently focused vault by default. Use `vault=<name>` as the first paramete
Use `--copy` on any command to copy output to clipboard. Use `silent` to prevent files from opening.
Run `obsidian help` to see all available commands. This is always up to date. Full docs: https://hel

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary JavaScript Evaluation In Obsidian

content.user_title: Manage Obsidian Vaults with CLI Commands
content.value_statement: Obsidian users need fast note operations without manual navigation. This skill uses the Obsidian CLI to read, update, search, and debug vaults.
actual_capabilities: Read active notes or named files through the Obsidian CLI.
Create notes, append content, update daily notes, and set note properties.
Search vault content, list tasks, sort tags, and review backlinks.
Target specific vaults and files with vault, file, or path parameters.
Reload plugins and inspect errors, console output, screenshots, DOM, and CSS.
Run Obsidian developer commands, including app-context JavaScript evaluation.
limitations: Obsidian must be open, and the Obsidian CLI must be installed.
Commands act on the focused vault unless a vault name is supplied.
Write commands can change local notes and should be reviewed first.
Developer commands depend on Obsidian version, plugins, and enabled debugging support.

use_cases.title: Review research notes
use_cases.description: Summarize active notes, find related notes, and add backlinks while preserving the vault structure.

use_cases.title: Maintain daily work logs
use_cases.description: Append tasks, update daily notes, search open items, and keep note properties current.

use_cases.title: Debug Obsidian plugins
use_cases.description: Reload plugins, inspect errors, capture screenshots, and review DOM or console output.

prompt_templates.title: Read Current Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the active Obsidian note and summarize the main sections, tasks, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Daily Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Append this task to today's daily note: [task]. Confirm the target vault and note before changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Search Related Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Search my vault for [topic], list the strongest matches, and suggest where a backlink should be added.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Plugin State
prompt_templates.prompt: Reload plugin [id], check errors and console output, inspect [selector], and report findings before editing code.

output_examples.input: Read my note named Project Plan.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a concise summary of sections, tasks, and open questions from that note.

output_examples.input: Add 'Schedule launch review' to today's daily note.
output_examples.output: The skill appends an unchecked task and reports the vault and note it changed.

output_examples.input: Check my plugin for errors after a rebuild.
output_examples.output: The skill reloads the plugin, checks Obsidian errors, and summarizes console or visual issues.

best_practices: Confirm the target vault and file before running read or write commands.
Use explicit file or path parameters when the active note is unclear.
Ask before using eval, screenshots, DOM inspection, clipboard output, or write commands.
anti_patterns: Do not run commands against an unspecified vault when multiple vaults are open.
Do not expose sensitive note content through broad searches, screenshots, or clipboard output.
Do not use JavaScript evaluation for routine note edits.

faq.question: Does this skill require Obsidian to be open?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill uses the Obsidian CLI against a running Obsidian instance.

faq.question: Can it create and update notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create notes, append content, update daily notes, and set properties.

faq.question: Can it work with multiple vaults?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply a vault name when the focused vault is not the intended target.

faq.question: Does it access the internet?
faq.answer: The documented workflow is local, but the skill links to Obsidian CLI documentation.

faq.question: Can it help plugin developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports reloads, error checks, screenshots, DOM inspection, CSS inspection, and console review.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Review write commands, eval commands, screenshots, clipboard output, DOM inspection, and target paths.
